# DXC issue triage — batch 018

**Ground truth:** local Debug compiler `main-debug`, registered at public commit
[`89e2f98e2`](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/commit/89e2f98e29c289ae8ad9e00dd310104fea9fd7df).
The binary self-reports `1.9.0.5465 (triage, 7665270b9)`, which is a fork-local
merge SHA that resolves for nobody else; the citation is the upstream commit the
source corresponds to. Equivalence was proven by tree rather than by hash:
`git diff --name-only origin/main HEAD` reports nothing outside
`.github/skills/dxc-issue-triage/`, and the `origin/main^` control does detect a
compiler-source difference, so the query can distinguish the two cases.

No DXC source was modified. **Nothing was posted, edited, labelled, closed or
reacted to on GitHub.**

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Sampling bias:** this batch is two issues, both named explicitly by the
> operator. They are the same defect seen from two directions — SPIR-V
> ray-query lowering under `-fspv-debug=vulkan-with-source` — and one is the
> other's duplicate. Two `close-fixed` verdicts out of two says nothing about
> the backlog's fixed rate, and this batch exercises no non-SPIR-V, no
> still-reproducing and no inconclusive path.

## Headline

- Both issues are `does-not-repro` with `complete` repros, both fixed in
  stable **v1.9.2602**, both recommended `close-fixed`. 7300 is already closed;
  **7033 is still open and is the actionable one.**
- The fixing commit was identified by **direct before/after measurement**, not
  by ancestry or PR linkage:
  [`61de7411f`](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/commit/61de7411f952cb0c4b6c73091555dad6419180ee)
  succeeds and its first parent `b0245e32f` still fails, on builds whose only
  source difference is that commit.
- One method observation was promoted into `triage.py`, and re-scoring moved
  **nine** archived probes across two issues — six of them in batch-014's 4501,
  which is exactly the retroactive propagation `reindex` exists to provide.

## Naming the fixing commit, by measurement

The stable sweep dates the fix to a release window; it cannot say what closed
it. Ancestry cannot either — it proves a commit is *present* in the fixing
release, not that it *is* the fix. So the candidate was built and run.

Two detached worktrees, at `61de7411f` and at its first parent
`b0245e32fdcf412850ed073476669f3a83fa5a76`, pin identical submodules, so the
only source difference between them is that commit's own 12-line diff
(`case SpirvType::TK_RayQueryKHR:` in `DebugTypeVisitor::lowerToDebugType`, plus
a regression test). Release `dxc` was built from each and never linked against
the shared build tree. Both binaries self-report their own commit
(`1.8.0.5092 (b0245e32f)`, `1.8.0.5093 (61de7411f)`), which is the in-file build
identity a crash-only probe otherwise lacks.

| build | 7033 repro | 7300 repro | control |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| parent `b0245e32f` | `0xE0000001` `Internal compiler error: LLVM Assert` | `0xE0000001` | exit 0 |
| commit `61de7411f` | exit 0 | exit 0, emits SPIR-V | exit 0 |

Each issue's control is its own: 7033 uses a shader with no `RayQuery`; 7300
uses the same command without `-fspv-debug=vulkan-with-source`. Both pass on
both builds, so the parent's failure is a property of ray-query debug-type
lowering rather than of the build. Captures are `manual-case-fix-commit.txt` in
each issue directory, generated by the committed `measure-fix-commit.py`, which
echoes every command through `subprocess.list2cmdline`.

**The parent fails as an assert (`0xE0000001`) where the shipped releases fail
as an access violation (`0xC0000005`).** Same defect, two signatures, one
`internal_failure` predicate — a predicate keyed to either message would have
scored half of this history wrong.

## Release-history cross-check

The blind re-derivation of 7033 (below) correctly flagged that no release
between v1.8.2505.1 and v1.9.2602 had been probed. The catalog closes it: there
is no such release. v1.8.2505.1 is built 2025-07-14 and v1.9.2602 is built
2026-02-20, with no stable tag and no prerelease in between, so the boundary is
as tight as stable releases allow. The commit-level measurement then narrows it
much further than any release could.

Both issues agree on the boundary independently, from different repros and
different profiles (`lib_6_4` for 7033, `cs_6_5` for 7300).

Their invalid probes are **not** the same set, and conflating them would be an
error: 7033's oldest four releases reject `-HV 2021`, while 7300's are
v1.4.1907 (`SPIR-V CodeGen not available`) plus v1.5.2010, v1.6.2104 and
v1.6.2106 rejecting the `vulkan-with-source` mode.

## Method lessons

**1. An unknown *value* of a recognised option is an invalid probe.**
(From `issues/7300/method-notes.md`.) v1.5.2010, v1.6.2104 and v1.6.2106 answer
`unknown SPIR-V debug info control parameter: vulkan-with-source` and exit 1.
They parsed `-fspv-debug` but could not express the requested mode, so they
never ran it — yet they scored as clean runs, which is the shape that invents a
fix boundary at whichever release learned the spelling. Every marker until now
named a *feature* the build lacks; this is the first that names a *value* it
lacks. Promoted into `UNSUPPORTED_MARKER_RE`, anchored to the observed SPIR-V
debug-info form and deliberately not generalised to `unknown ... parameter`,
which would demote ordinary diagnostics. A negative control asserting that
`too few arguments for parameter 'x'` is *not* demoted ships with it.

`reindex --accept` then restamped nine headers: three in 7300 and six in 4501
(primary and `match-instrument` captures). **No verdict changed.** 4501's
history is `never-implemented` over the 16 releases from v1.6.2112 that can emit
`NonSemantic.Shader.DebugInfo.100`, and the three demoted releases were already
outside that population; its notes table has been corrected to say
`invalid-probe`, so no artifact still describes the old scoring. Measurements
were untouched.

**2. A second copy of a predicate drifts silently, and this one had.**
`test_predicates.py` carried its own literal copy of the feature-absence regex
while importing `triage` anyway. The copy had already lost three markers that
`triage.py` has — `for non-scalar types use 'select'`, the anchored
`is not supported (for|on|in|with) (target|profile|shader model|stage)` form,
and the `unknown HLSL version:` value capture — so the suite was passing against
a regex the classifier does not use. The pattern is now a module-level
`triage.UNSUPPORTED_MARKER_RE` that the test imports. Worth generalising: a test
that restates the thing under test tests itself.

**3. Attribute a fix by building it, or say you did not.**
The window here was one commit wide only because it was measured; before that,
the honest statement was the release boundary. `SKILL.md` already says to call
an ancestry-based attribution strong rather than certain — this batch is the
worked example of paying the build cost instead, and of the two controls that
make the result mean what it says.

`issues/7033/method-notes.md` does not exist; that worker recorded no method
observation. The audit does not require one, but its absence is why lesson 1
rests on a single worker's report rather than on two independent sightings.

## Evidence verification

- `reindex` rebuilt 107 issues and 2,092 runs. After the promotion above and
  `--accept`, the only remaining report was the two pending `reviewed_by`
  fields, now filled.
- `test_predicates.py` passes, including the two new marker cases.
- `check_paths.py` passes: 5,401 committable text files, 16 allowlisted matches
  in 4 files, no unexpected machine paths. The new `measure-fix-commit.py`
  rewrites each build tree to a `<label>-worktree>` placeholder derived from the
  case label, so its captures carry no machine layout.
- `audit --issue` is clean for both issues.
- **Cross-reference timeline check.** 7033 carries three pre-existing events
  (2025-02-12 `#7139`, 2025-04-02 `#7300`, 2025-04-04 `#7311`) and 7300 carries
  one (2025-04-02 `#7033`). Every event predates this batch by more than a year;
  **no cross-reference on either issue was created by this branch.** The commit
  message for this batch uses bare issue numbers.
- The temporary worktrees and their build trees were removed;
  `git worktree list` shows no leftover, and no shared build target was rebuilt
  or relinked.

## Independent checks

**Blind re-derivation (7033, `claude-sonnet-5`).** Required because the
suggested action is `close-fixed`. Given the issue directory without
`notes.md`, `verdict.json` or `comment.md`, it independently reproduced the
status, the v1.8.2505.1 → v1.9.2602 boundary, the four `-HV 2021` invalid
probes, and the `close-fixed` recommendation — and flagged the unprobed release
window, which the catalog shows is empty.

**Draft review (`gpt-5.6-sol`), briefed with the evidence files as well as the
drafts.** It found **no factual or arithmetic error**: every exit code, release
tag, commit SHA and quantifier checked out against the captures, and both
fixing-commit claims matched what `manual-case-fix-commit.txt` measured. Its
three proposals were all concision and all accepted:

- 7033 said Compiler Explorer showed "the transition". It shows two endpoints;
  it does not locate a transition. Corrected — and worth keeping in mind, since
  CE's oldest DXC is 1.6.2112 and cannot date anything older.
- Both drafts announced that the commit attribution was "measured, not
  inferred" immediately before describing the measurement. Cut from both; the
  measurement is the claim.

`triaged_by=GPT-5.4`, `reviewed_by=GPT-5.6 Sol` recorded on both issues.

## `text_stale`

**7033 is marked stale and should be:** filed 2024-12-12, its title still says
ray queries do not work with `-fspv-debug=vulkan-with-source`, and the issue is
**open**, so a reader spot-checking it today meets a title the compiler
contradicts.

**7300 is deliberately not marked stale.** Its text was accurate when filed and
the issue is already closed as a duplicate, so there is no open description
misleading anyone. Staleness is a claim about someone's writing and is held to
a high bar; "was overtaken by a later fix" is not staleness.

Both `summary` fields were re-read sentence by sentence against `notes.md`.
Each now names the measured commit and its parent, which the evidence supports
directly; neither asserts anything the long-form notes do not.

## Proposed issue comments

These are **drafts for review, not posted**. No comment, label or state change
has been made on any issue. Each is written to be postable as-is by a maintainer, and every
claim in them is backed by captured evidence in `issues/<nnnn>/`.

They deliberately avoid promising fixes or timelines, and where the next step is a product or
language decision they say so rather than pre-empting it. Quoted compiler output was
re-verified before being written down.

Each draft ends with a trailer disclosing that it came from an assisted triage pass.

Source of each is `issues/<nnnn>/comment.md` — edit there, then re-run
`scripts/render_comments.py <batch>` to refresh this section.


### Draft — [#7033](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/7033) [SPIR-V] Ray queries do not work with -fspv-debug=vulkan-with-source

````markdown
> [!WARNING]
> **Draft — not a maintainer decision.** AI-assisted triage for
> [#7033](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/7033).

This is fixed on current `main` (source-equivalent to
`89e2f98e29c289ae8ad9e00dd310104fea9fd7df`; the local Debug binary self-reports
`7665270b9`). The exact filed command now exits 0 and emits rich debug information for the
ray-query variable.

Stable-release testing places the fix in **v1.9.2602**: v1.8.2505.1 still access-violates,
while v1.9.2602 compiles successfully.
[Compiler Explorer](https://godbolt.org/z/EbMbKx9d9) shows dxc 1.6.2112 terminating with
SIGSEGV, while trunk succeeds.

Release `dxc` built at
[`61de7411f`](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/commit/61de7411f952cb0c4b6c73091555dad6419180ee)
("lower spirv ray query type to opaque debug type") compiles the filed command
successfully, while the same build at its parent `b0245e32f` fails it with
`0xE0000001` (`Internal compiler error: LLVM Assert`). A control shader with no
`RayQuery` compiles on both, so the failure is specific to ray-query debug-type
lowering.

The existing `bug` and `spirv` labels remain accurate; no label change is suggested. The
issue can be closed as fixed.
````

### Draft — [#7300](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/7300) [SPIR-V] Failed to compile ray query shader with  -fspv-debug=vulkan-with-source

````markdown
> [!WARNING]
> **Draft — not a maintainer decision.** AI-assisted triage for
> [#7300](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/7300).

This complete repro is fixed on current main
(`89e2f98e29c289ae8ad9e00dd310104fea9fd7df`). The as-filed command exits 0 and
emits SPIR-V; the local Debug binary self-reports fork-local merge `7665270b9`.

The stable-release boundary is v1.8.2505.1 → v1.9.2602:

```text
v1.8.2505.1: exit 0xC0000005
Internal compiler error: access violation. Attempted to read from address 0x0000000000000008

v1.9.2602: exit 0
; SPIR-V
```

[Compiler Explorer](https://godbolt.org/z/zbP5qasd3) likewise shows DXC
1.6.2112 terminating with `SIGSEGV` and trunk compiling successfully.

The fix is commit
[`61de7411f`](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/commit/61de7411f952cb0c4b6c73091555dad6419180ee)
("lower spirv ray query type to opaque debug type"). Building Release `dxc` at
that commit and at its parent `b0245e32f`,
the parent fails the as-filed command with `0xE0000001`
(`Internal compiler error: LLVM Assert`) while the commit exits 0 and emits
SPIR-V. Dropping `-fspv-debug=vulkan-with-source` makes both builds exit 0, so
the failure is specific to ray-query debug-type lowering.

I suggest adding `crash` and removing `needs-triage`; this issue is already closed.

---
<sub>Triaged with AI assistance. Compiler output was produced by running the repro; please
flag anything that looks wrong.</sub>
````

## Caveats

- Drafts are unposted and require maintainer review. Nothing was applied to any
  issue, including the label proposals on 7300 (`+crash`, `-needs-triage`).
- Two issues, one defect, operator-selected. No general conclusion follows.
- The commit-level result is a Release build measurement on Windows x64. It
  brackets the behaviour change; it does not establish that no other change in
  the same release also mattered to some other manifestation.
- `manual-case-fix-commit.txt` is a harness capture, not a `run` probe, so
  `reindex` does not re-score it. It is regenerable from the committed
  `measure-fix-commit.py` given the two builds.
